description: Which check guards which file. The single source for the coverage record: docs-testing.md points at this file instead of restating it, test/coverage.test.js keeps it honest, and AI/claude/hooks/name-covering-checks.mjs reads it to name the checks when a guarded file is edited. Paths are relative to the repository root.

test/smoke.test.js.what: The harness itself: both roles reach authenticated content, two sessions stay independent in either order, and the two sessions really are different users.

test/content.test.js.what: Wiring for the content suite: imports every check module so the whole suite runs in one process, and asserts that a run logs in once per role.

test/checks/permissions.js.what: Block-level and whole-file directives in both directions, including the admin directive and both plural aliases (teachers and students), their effect on the navigation tree, time-bounded windows, and the teacher-to-student downgrade.

test/checks/views.js.what: The #exam, #practice and #answer pseudo-roles, driven through the ve and va preferences.

test/checks/rendering.js.what: Callouts and their collapsible forms, highlighted code, fragment indices, side-by-side columns, the image forms, and the emitted PlantUML and Mermaid markup.

test/checks/navigation.js.what: Wiki-link resolution including the duplicated basename — with a digit in the name and without one — and the name with spaces, the folder-name edge cases, the table of contents and the navigation tree.
corpus: md/folder-tests/a very long folder with spaces oh my god i cannot believe how long it is/Untitled.md

test/checks/presentation.js.what: The deck built from the source's heading structure, fragments in a deck, the deck's own references including the known-dangling list, that it contacts no host but the application and the identity provider, that a host a stylesheet asks for is recorded even when refused, the document view, and the documented shortcut into it with the shift key held and without.

test/checks/deployment-surface.js.what: What a running instance publishes over HTTP: that keycloak.json, the application sources, the dependency manifests and what sits beside a mounted package directory are not served and a refusal looks like a path with no file behind it, that the assets a page addresses still are — including the ones only a stylesheet names — that every same-origin reference of a rendered page resolves in all three views, and that the one endpoint answering before authentication survives a parameter it cannot interpret.

test/coverage.test.js.what: The coverage record itself: every path it names exists, every test file appears in it, and no entry names a file that is gone.
